AfterObtained.rationale: STALE rollup, same failure mode as this batch's relic/burning_sticks/AfterCardExhausted and relic/electric_shrymp/AfterObtained: it aggregates G1 and G2 per binding rule 4, but G1 -- the pool-ORDER bug this rollup was written to describe -- was closed 2026-07-29 (round 6): events/neow.py's `neow_relic_pool` now appends the six singleton relics in Neow.cs's own AllPossibleOptions order, and `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b10.py neows-bones` RE-EXECUTED today prints 'tails equal: True' with 0 divergent seeds (was 24/60). What remains under this rollup is only G2 -- the missing reward-SCREEN wrapper around an otherwise-unconditional grant -- which was never a 'gap' in the first place: its own guard entry below is `deliberate-divergence`, on the basis that `WithSkippingDisallowed` (RewardsSet.cs:115) has exactly one caller in the whole source, this relic, so Neow's Bones is the only non-declinable relic offer in the game and the sim's unconditional grant reaches the identical observable (same two relics, same order, no skip possible). With G1 closed and G2 never a live gap, this hook-level entry has no citable divergence left under 'gap'; re-verdicted to match the worst remaining guard rather than left stale.  The text it replaced: "Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The SHAPE is right -- two relics drawn from Neow's own option pool on the per-player Rewards stream, then one generatable curse on the Niche stream -- and the shuffle algorithm, the curse pool and the curse ordering all match. What does not match is the relic pool's ORDER (G1), which changes which two relics come out."

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the sim's Neow pool lists the three coin-flip PAIRS where C#'s AllPossibleOptions lists the six relics individually, so the shuffled Take(2) draws different relics
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 6): the pool order matches. Neow.AllPossibleOptions (Neow.cs:53-62) adds the six non-paired relics ONE AT A TIME -- LavaRock, NeowsTalisman, NutritiousOyster, Pomander, SmallCapsule, StoneHumidifier -- and events/neow.py's `neow_relic_pool` now appends exactly that tuple (`_SINGLETON_OPTIONS`) instead of the three coin-flip PAIRS. The pairing is a fact about GenerateInitialOptions' NextBool flips, not about the pool, and it is still used there. EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b10.py neows-bones` now prints `tails equal: True` and finds 0 divergent seeds where it found 24 of 60. One legacy test moved with it: test_neows_bones asserted `len(ids) == 3`, which held only under the wrong order -- seed 12 now draws Cursed Pearl, whose own AfterObtained pulls a further relic, so the test pins the two PICKS instead of a total.  The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: NeowsBones.cs:40-42 takes `GetValidRelics(...).ToList()`, calls `PlayerRng.Rewards.Shuffle(list)` and then `.Take(2)`. A Fisher-Yates shuffle's swap INDICES depend only on the RNG, so the output depends entirely on the INPUT ORDER -- the pool order is load-bearing. Neow.AllPossibleOptions (Neow.cs:49-64) is CurseOptions (8, Neow.cs:96-106) + PositiveOptions (14, Neow.cs:66-82) + LavaRock, NeowsTalisman, NutritiousOyster, Pomander, SmallCapsule, StoneHumidifier as six SEPARATE trailing options (Neow.cs:84-94, in that declaration order). events/neow.py:64-72 instead appends the three coin-flip PAIRS -- (lava_rock, small_capsule), (nutritious_oyster, stone_humidifier), (neows_talisman, pomander) -- giving the trailing six in a different order. The first 19 entries match exactly. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b10.py neows-bones): Rng.Shuffle (Rng.cs:308-320) and the sim's shuffle (rng.py:270-273) are the same top-down Fisher-Yates, so only the order can differ; over 60 string seeds the two orders yield DIFFERENT pairs on 24 of them, e.g. seed B10SEED06 gives ['stone_humidifier','precarious_shears'] in the sim and ['pomander','precarious_shears'] in the game, and seed B10SEED11 gives ['small_capsule','lava_rock'] vs ['neows_talisman','lava_rock']. LIVE: Neow's Bones is one of the eight ported Neow curse options (events/neow.py:45-48), every run visits the Neow node, and the two relics it grants run their own AfterObtained pickup effects -- so a wrong pair changes max HP, gold, the deck and the relic list from floor 0 onward. Not pre-diagnosed by any sweep. Rule 7: Neow.cs, Rng.cs, events/neow.py, rng.py and run.py are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: G2: `new RewardsSet(Owner).WithCustomRewards(...).WithSkippingDisallowed().Offer()` (NeowsBones.cs:43) is a reward SCREEN; the port grants both relics unconditionally
guards.rationale: STILL a deliberate-divergence after the 2026-07-26 fix pass re-verdicted the rest of the auto-keep cluster to gap, and this record is the REASON the cluster is a cluster: `grep -rn WithSkippingDisallowed src/` returns exactly two lines in the whole source -- the definition (RewardsSet.cs:115) and its single caller, NeowsBones.cs:43 -- so Neow's Bones is the ONLY non-declinable relic offer in the game. The player therefore has no choice to make here and the sim's unconditional grant reaches the same observable: the same two relics land in the same order, and no `wasPicked:false` history entry is written because RelicReward.OnSkipped (RelicReward.cs:117-123) can never run. The only thing lost is the screen. (Previously this entry justified itself by citing relic/calling_bell G3's 'house rule for non-choice relic offers'; that rationale is gone -- CallingBell.cs:31 is a plain skippable `RewardsCmd.OfferCustom` and calling_bell G3 is now a gap. The verdict here survives on `WithSkippingDisallowed` alone, which is a stronger basis than the one it replaced.) Residual, and the reason this is not simply faithful: C# runs each relic's `AfterObtained` inside `RelicReward.OnSelect` (RelicReward.cs:109-115) as the player confirms each card, whereas `run.add_relic` (sts2_rl/run.py) fires it at grant time -- with skipping disallowed both orders end at the same state. Flagged so that whoever fixes G1 does not silently harden the auto-keep. Rule 7: src/Core/Rewards/RewardsSet.cs, src/Core/Rewards/RelicReward.cs and sts2_rl/run.py are cited and not all hashed here.

guards.what: N1: the shuffle primitive and the Take(2) slice
guards.rationale: EXECUTED (relic_probes_b10.py neows-bones): Rng.Shuffle (Rng.cs:308-320) walks `for (num = Count-1; num > 0; num--) swap(num, NextInt(num+1))` and the sim's rng.py:270-273 is byte-identical in structure, so with the same stream and the same input the permutations agree. neows_bones.py:27-29 shuffles then slices `pool[:self.RELICS]`, matching `.Take(2)`.

neow_relic_pool (events/neow.py:64-72) applies the same is_allowed_at_neow filter and neows_bones.py:22 excludes the relic's own id. Executed pool size 25 (of 8+14+6=28 minus self, kaleidoscope and massive_scroll). NOTE A CROSS-UNIT DEPENDENCY: .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md Sweep B records that relic/scroll_boxes leaves is_allowed_at_neow at True where C# gates on CanGenerateBundles(player) -- if that turns out to exclude Scroll Boxes, this pool loses an entry and G1's divergence changes shape. That is scroll_boxes' own record to settle, not this one's. Rule 7: events/neow.py, relics/scroll_boxes.py and the sweeps document are unhashed here.

guards.what: N3: the curse half -- `CurseCardPool.GetUnlockedCards(...)` filtered by CanBeGeneratedByModifiers, `orderby c.Id`, then Rng.Niche.NextItem with removal (NeowsBones.cs:44-55)
guards.rationale: EXECUTED (relic_probes_b10.py neows-bones). CurseCardPool declares 18 curses (CurseCardPool.cs:18-41) and the sim's generatable curse list is 10 (cards/pool.py:70-78 applies exactly the CanBeGeneratedByModifiers filter). neows_bones.py:30-34 sorts the ids, draws with `run.rng_set.niche.next_item(...)` -- the SAME Niche stream C# names -- and removes the pick before the next iteration, matching NeowsBones.cs:51-52. The `orderby c.Id` key is C#'s uppercase ModelId while the sim sorts lowercase ids, which can flip order when '_' meets a letter ('_' sorts after Z but before a); executed for this pool it does not, because no generatable curse id contains an underscore (['clumsy','debt','decay','doubt','guilty','injury','normality','regret','shame','writhe'] sorts identically either way). `GetUnlockedCards`'s UnlockState argument is waived: the sim assumes full unlocks (a grep for UnlockState over sts2_rl/ returns nothing), which is the same treatment relic/lasting_candy's record gives it. Rule 7: CurseCardPool.cs, cards/pool.py and relics/lasting_candy.py are unhashed here.

guards.what: N4: the legacy (non-parity) `else` branch (neows_bones.py:35-40) uses the shared run rng and `random_curses(distinct=True)` instead of the ordered Niche draw
guards.rationale: The repo-wide convention: `run.rng_set is None` means an RL run with no string seed, and every ported unit keeps its pre-SP2 draw sequence byte-for-byte on that path so training/eval numbers do not move (run.py states this for the RNG seating; relics/arcane_scroll.py:27-30 is the same if/else shape). The audited path is the parity one. Recorded rather than skipped because a reader diffing only the else-branch would see an unordered curse pick and file it as a gap.
